appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.pedice.why: A cluster's flower stands on a stalk as long, for the length of the cluster and its peduncle, as floras measure them.

appearance.organs.flower.inflorescence.why: A flower borne in a cluster of known length is drawn as the cluster, its units laid out by the cluster rules; a solitary flower stays one flower, and so does one whose cluster's length no source gives.

appearance.organs.bloom.inflorescence.why: A tree's or shrub's flowers borne in clusters of known length are drawn as the clusters; solitary flowers stay single.

appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.unit.why: A cluster's flower is as wide, for the length of the cluster and its peduncle, as floras measure them, whichever axis bears it: a panicle's or compound umbel's flowers sit on its branches. Where no flower size is stated its units are as long as its fruit, which ripen in their place.

generator.params.flower_size.why: A herb's flowering organ is as long as its inflorescence and the peduncle it stands on where its flowers are in clusters, else as wide as its flower.

generator.params.bloom_size.why: A tree's or shrub's bloom is as long as its inflorescence and the peduncle it stands on where its flowers are in clusters, else as wide as its flower.

appearance.organs.flower.colour.why: An open flower is drawn in the colour its showiest part is stated in.

appearance.organs.bloom.colour.why: A tree's or shrub's blooms are drawn in the colour its flowers' showiest part is stated in.

appearance.organs.fruit.colour.why: A fruit is drawn in the colour it is stated to ripen to; its unripe share keeps the look's accent.

appearance.organs.fruit.shape.aspect.why: A fruit is as wide for its length as its flora measures it.

appearance.organs.fruit.accent.why: A fruit's unripe share, and its stalk, are drawn in the green of the plant's leaves until a colour of its own is stated.

appearance.organs.fruit.inflorescence.un.why: A cluster's fruit is as long, for the length of the cluster and its peduncle, as floras measure them, whichever axis bears it.

appearance.organs.*.season.flower_look.s.why: A flower is as wide, for its fruit's length, as floras measure the flower and the fruit: a cluster's flower against its fruit, a lone flower against the fruit it becomes.

appearance.organs.*.season.fruit_size.why: A lone flower's organ is grown as wide as its flower, so its fruit is drawn at the fruit's stated length; a cluster grown as long as its inflorescence grows in fruit where its fruit outgrow it, to hold them on their stalks (a third again their length, as an umbel's rays need).

appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.kind.why: Each kind of inflorescence is laid out as the cluster of its name, and a spadix as a spike; a solitary flower is no cluster.

appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.flower.why: A cluster bears the inflorescence's units, up to the 200 an axis can hold; a compound one shares them among its primary branches, so it needs their count.

appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.branch.why: A compound cluster bears the inflorescence's primary branches, up to 60.

appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.dome.why: A flat-topped corymb's flowers stand level; a rounded one's lie on a half sphere, a globose one's round a ball.

appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.droop.why: An erect inflorescence's axis stays straight; a nodding one bends over by a quarter turn toward its tip, a pendent one by half a turn, so it hangs.

appearance.organs.*.shape.pattern.why: A compound leaf sets its leaflets along a rachis or from the petiole's tip, as its division pattern says.

A leaf divided once bears none.

appearance.organs.*.shape.segments.why: Each pinnule of a thrice-divided leaf bears the leaflets or segments floras count on it, odd or even as it ends, where floras count its pinnules too. A leaf divided once or twice has none.

appearance.organs.*.shape.inner.why: A compound leaf whose later divisions are set otherwise than its first (a ternate-pinnate leaf) draws them as its inner division pattern says.

appearance.organs.*.shape.blade_width.why: A pinnate leaf's laterals reach no farther than the blade's edge, its width over its length as floras measure them: a strap-shaped leaf's pinnae are short for their spacing.

appearance.organs.*.shape.lace.why: A divided leaf whose taxa say how its divisions are held is drawn up close as geometry, its rachises and each leaflet or segment where it stands, on the two nearest levels; farther off, on its card.

appearance.organs.*.shape.lift.why: A spray's primary divisions rise a quarter of a right angle out of the leaf's plane; a flat leaf's and a bottlebrush's do not.

appearance.organs.*.shape.scatter.why: Each division turns a little at random about its rachis: hardly in a flat leaf, up to 30 degrees either way in a spray, 20 round a bottlebrush.

appearance.organs.*.shape.roll.why: A bottlebrush's primary divisions turn round the rachis by the golden angle from one to the next, so they stand all round it; a flat leaf's and a spray's keep two ranks.

appearance.organs.*.shape.inner_roll.why: A bottlebrush's leaflets or segments turn round their division's rachis by the golden angle too; a flat leaf's and a spray's lie in their division's plane.

appearance.organs.*.shape.confluent.why: A blade dissected into fine segments is drawn as a divided leaf whose segments run together along a winged rachis; a compound leaf's leaflets stand apart.

appearance.organs.*.shape.perianth.why: A calyx and corolla draws one whorl of petals with sepals below them; like tepals draw two whorls; a spiral, tepals on a spiral; no perianth, none.

appearance.organs.*.shape.petal_ratio.why: A petal is as wide for its length as its outline is stated: a narrow strap (linear) to as broad as long (orbicular), drawn among as many petals as the flower has.

appearance.organs.*.shape.taper.why: A petal narrows from its widest to its tip as its outline is stated: straight sides to a point (lanceolate, ovate), a curve (elliptic), or round and full to the tip (obovate, spatulate, orbicular, oblong).

appearance.organs.*.shape.point.why: A petal's tip is as pointed as stated: drawn out (acuminate), pointed (acute), blunt (obtuse), or round (rounded, truncate, and a notched tip's lobes).

appearance.organs.*.shape.notch.why: An emarginate petal's tip is notched; a bilobed one is cleft into two lobes.

appearance.organs.*.shape.petals.why: A flower draws its merosity's petals, twice it in tepals, or a spiral's tepals in all, up to 60.

appearance.organs.*.shape.sepals.why: A calyx has as many sepals as the flower's merosity; tepals and a spiral's outer tepals are drawn as the perianth itself.

appearance.organs.*.shape.corolla.why: A zygomorphic flower's parts differ by place as its zygomorphy says, and one of no named kind draws its upper petal unlike the rest, wider and more upright; a regular flower, even in a family whose zygomorphic flowers are of a kind, is drawn with its petals alike.

appearance.organs.*.shape.fused.why: A bell, funnel, tube or urn is a corolla whose petals are joined for that share of their length; a flat or cupped one has them free.

appearance.organs.*.shape.throat.why: A tube's mouth, over a petal's length: wide for a bell, narrow for a tube, narrower for a salver's or an urn's.

appearance.organs.*.shape.belly.why: An urn swells in its middle and narrows to its mouth.

appearance.organs.*.shape.tube.why: A hypanthium is a floral cup under the perianth, 0.4 of the flower's radius long.

appearance.organs.*.shape.ovary.why: The ovary sits inside the whorls, half below them, or below them.

appearance.organs.*.shape.turn.why: A resupinate flower is drawn turned half round, so a lip formed toward the axis hangs below.

appearance.organs.*.shape.anther_tilt.why: An anther stands along its filament where the filament joins its base, leans where it joins its back, and lies nearly across the filament's tip where it swings free (versatile), as Simpson defines the three.

appearance.organs.*.shape.stamens.why: A flower draws its stamens, up to 200.

appearance.organs.*.shape.staminodes.why: A flower draws its sterile stamens without anthers, up to 50.

appearance.organs.*.shape.carpels.why: A flower draws one pistil of up to five carpels, or of any number in an inferior ovary; above five in a superior one, as many free pistils, up to 30.

generator.params.fruit_length.why: A herb's fruit is as long as floras measure it at its longest.

generator.params.fruit_size.why: A fruit is as long as floras measure it at its longest.

appearance.organs.*.shape.kind.why: A berry or drupe is drawn as an ellipsoid, and so is a dry one-seeded fruit (an achene, cypsela, grain or nut) in its own dull colour; a pome dimpled at its top; a capsule, follicle or schizocarp ribbed lengthwise; a legume or other pod long, flat and bulging over its seeds; a samara as a seed at the base of a wing; an aggregate or multiple fruit as a cluster of drupelets. A nut's cup or husk and a berry's crown are the lineage's to say.

appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.pedunc.why: A cluster stands on a bare stalk, its peduncle, its share of the stalk and the cluster together; a cluster's units or branches begin above it. Where no peduncle is stated the organ is the cluster alone, as long as floras measure it from its lowest unit or branch, so its units begin at its foot.

appearance.organs.*.shape.spur.why: A spur is drawn as long as its length over the flower's radius, up to three radii.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.template.why: A leaf of separate leaflets is drawn on a compound card, whose pattern the leaf rules set; a blade cut from one point on a palmate card, one cut along its midrib on a lobed card, and an uncut one on a simple card.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.template.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated. A leaf of separate leaflets is drawn on a compound card, whose pattern the leaf rules set; a blade cut from one point on a palmate card, one cut along its midrib on a lobed card, and an uncut one on a simple card.

appearance.organs.bloom.shape.template.why: Single flowers are drawn on a flower card, heads of florets on a head card and spikelets on a spikelet card; the inflorescence rules lay them out. A flowering plant whose taxa do not say is drawn with single flowers.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.template.why: Single flowers are drawn on a flower card, heads of florets on a head card and spikelets on a spikelet card; the inflorescence rules lay them out. A flowering plant whose taxa do not say is drawn with single flowers.

appearance.organs.*.season.why: A plant whose flowering and fruiting months are stated flowers and fruits in them: each flowering look its files leave without a year is a bud, a flower and fruit on the days its months give, and gone outside them. A flower's look becomes its look in flower and its own look its fruit, which the fruit's rules draw; a head or a spikelet is drawn as itself in each stage.

appearance.organs.*.season.bud.why: A look's buds show half a month before the first month it flowers in; for one that flowers from January, in the December before, its whole year counted from then.

appearance.organs.*.season.flower.why: Its first flowers open as the first month it flowers in begins.

appearance.organs.*.season.opening.why: A cluster still flowering in the months its first fruit are ripe opens its flowers one after another over those months, so it flowers to the end of its months while its first fruit ripen.

appearance.organs.*.season.ripe.rule: max(max(month_start(min(flowering_months)) + 1, (opening > 0 ? month_start(max(flowering_months) + 1) : min(month_start(max(flowering_months) + 1), max(month_start(min(fruiting_months) + (min(fruiting_months) < min(flowering_months) ? 12 : 0)), round((month_start(max(flowering_months) + 1) + month_start(min(fruiting_months) + (min(fruiting_months) < min(flowering_months) ? 12 : 0))) / 2)))) - opening), (opening > 0 ? month_start(min(fruiting_months) + (min(fruiting_months) < min(flowering_months) ? 12 : 0)) : max(min(month_start(max(flowering_months) + 1), max(month_start(min(fruiting_months) + (min(fruiting_months) < min(flowering_months) ? 12 : 0)), round((month_start(max(flowering_months) + 1) + month_start(min(fruiting_months) + (min(fruiting_months) < min(flowering_months) ? 12 : 0))) / 2))), month_start(min(fruiting_months) + (min(fruiting_months) < min(flowering_months) ? 12 : 0)))) - ripening / 2) + (min(flowering_months) == 1 ? 365 : 0)
appearance.organs.*.season.ripe.why: Its fruit is half ripe as the first month it is ripe in begins (one before its flowers' is in the next year), or where its last flowers are still open then, as they go to fruit; it ripens only once it is fruit.

appearance.organs.*.season.fall.why: Its fruit falls as the last month it is ripe in ends, within a year of its buds.

rules.generator.params.fruit_length.note: How PlantGen sizes a fruit (morphology terms to drawing rules, 2026-10-16): a herb's fruit card is as long as the stated ripe fruit at its longest (fruit_size_m), where before every herb drew the program's 6 cm.

rules.generator.params.fruit_size.note: How PlantGen sizes a fruit (morphology terms to drawing rules, 2026-10-16): a climber's, column's or epiphyte's fruit is as long as the stated ripe fruit at its longest (fruit_size_m).

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.kind.note: Ingrouille's fruit types (pp. 162-163 of the PDF), with Simpson's Moraceae multiples: an achene, a cypsela (an achene from an inferior ovary) and a caryopsis (a grain) are small dry one-seeded fruits that do not open, a nut the same with a hard wall, so each is drawn as a plain ellipsoid; a schizocarp splits lengthwise into one-seeded mericarps, drawn ribbed lengthwise as a capsule; an aggregate fruit comes from the many free pistils of one flower and a multiple fruit from the flowers of a whole inflorescence, each a cluster of small fleshy units, drawn as drupelets.

rules.generator.params.flower_size.note: How PlantGen draws a flower borne in a cluster, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 4, 2026-10-15): the flowering organ is the cluster, as long as floras measure the inflorescence, its flowers as wide as they measure the flower, laid out by the cluster kind the taxa state.

rules.generator.params.bloom_size.note: How PlantGen draws a flower borne in a cluster, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 4, 2026-10-15): the flowering organ is the cluster, as long as floras measure the inflorescence, its flowers as wide as they measure the flower, laid out by the cluster kind the taxa state.

rules.appearance.organs.flower.colour.note: How PlantGen colours an organ from the colour a source states for the species, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 3, 2026-10-14): the stated colour itself, on the looks' 0 to 1 scale.

rules.appearance.organs.bloom.colour.note: How PlantGen colours an organ from the colour a source states for the species, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 3, 2026-10-14): the stated colour itself, on the looks' 0 to 1 scale.

rules.appearance.organs.fruit.colour.note: How PlantGen colours an organ from the colour a source states for the species, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 3, 2026-10-14): the stated colour itself, on the looks' 0 to 1 scale.

rules.appearance.organs.fruit.shape.aspe.note: How PlantGen draws a fruit from the measures a source states for the species, a choice of the model's: its width over its length, as the fruit card's aspect.

rules.appearance.organs.*.season.note: How PlantGen draws a plant's year from the months floras give, a choice of the model's (seasonal looks, 2026-10-16): its flowers show in the months it flowers in and its fruit in the months it is ripe in, as the season rules set their days, where they had shown all year and never fruited.

rules.appearance.organs.fruit.accent.note: How PlantGen colours unripe fruit, a choice of the model's (seasonal looks, 2026-10-16): green as the leaves are, since floras state the ripe colour and seldom the unripe one.

rules.appearance.organs.*.inflorescence..note: How PlantGen draws a corymb's outline, a choice of the model's (batch 3 review, 2026-10-18): floras word a corymb flat-topped, rounded (convex) or globose, as Dendrology (2019) p. 323 does a mophead hydrangea's; the three are drawn as tips level, on a half sphere and round a ball.

rules.appearance.organs.fruit.infloresce.note: How PlantGen draws a cluster in fruit, a choice of the model's (seasonal looks, 2026-10-16): each fruit as long, for the cluster's length, as floras measure the fruit, as its flowers are drawn as wide as they measure the flower.

rules.appearance.organs.*.season.flower_.note: How PlantGen sizes a flower against its fruit, a choice of the model's (seasonal looks, 2026-10-16): a stage's look is sized as a share of the organ in fruit, so a flower is the ratio of the stated flower and fruit sizes (flower_size_m, fruit_size_m), whether it is a cluster's unit or a lone flower.

rules.appearance.organs.*.season.opening.note: How PlantGen draws a cluster that flowers and fruits at once, a choice of the model's (seasonal looks, 2026-10-16): where the stated fruiting months (fruiting_months) begin before the flowering months (flowering_months) end, a cluster's units open one after another from the first ripe month to the end of flowering, so the plant shows flowers and ripe fruit together as the floras describe.

rules.appearance.organs.*.season.fruit_s.note: How PlantGen sizes an organ in fruit, a choice of the model's (seasonal looks, 2026-10-16): the programs grow a lone flowering organ as wide as its flower (flower_size_m) and a cluster as long as its inflorescence (inflorescence_length_m), so in fruit the organ is scaled to the stated fruit (fruit_size_m): a lone one by the ratio of fruit to flower, a cluster only where its fruit outgrow it, to 1.3 times the fruit's length, the room an umbel's rays leave a unit on its stalk.

traits.reproduction.note: The angiosperms are the flowering plants: their ovules sit inside an ovary, and their seeds ripen in a fruit (Biology 2e, 26.3).

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.pattern.note: How PlantGen draws a divided leaf, a choice of the model's (spec rework P4): the leaf characters set a compound card's pattern, its leaflets or pinnae, the leaflets on each pinna, and whether its segments run together. A pinnate leaf's count says how it ends (odd-pinnate odd, even-pinnate even), so a flora's range is drawn as the nearest count of the right kind.

A pinnate leaf's count says how it ends (odd-pinnate odd, even-pinnate even), so a flora's range is drawn as the nearest count of the right kind.

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.blade_wi.note: How PlantGen fits a divided leaf's laterals to its blade, a choice of the model's (lacy leaves, 2026-10-17): a flora's leaf length and width bound the blade, so a lateral standing at its angle to the rachis reaches no farther than the width allows. The middle of each range is read.

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.lace.note: How PlantGen draws a divided leaf's divisions in three dimensions, a choice of the model's (lacy leaves, 2026-10-17): iNaturalist photos of yarrow, lomatiums and fennel show their segments spread in several planes, and FEIS (Aleksoff 1999) describes native yarrows' narrow segments as set in various planes, making the leaf three-dimensional. The angles are set by eye from the photos.

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.confluen.note: How PlantGen draws a divided leaf, a choice of the model's (spec rework P4): the leaf characters set a compound card's pattern, its leaflets or pinnae, the leaflets on each pinna, and whether its segments run together. A pinnate leaf's count says how it ends (odd-pinnate odd, even-pinnate even), so a flora's range is drawn as the nearest count of the right kind.

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.perianth.note: How PlantGen draws a flower, a choice of the model's (spec rework P5): the flower characters set a flower card's perianth, its parts, how they differ by place, how far the corolla is joined into a tube, a floral cup, where the ovary sits, a resupinate flower's turn, its stamens, staminodes and carpels and its spurs. The rules also set these fields in a season's flower and bud looks that draw a flower, unless set there by hand.

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.petal_ra.note: The chart of plane shapes sets each outline word by its length-to-width ratio and where it is widest; a petal or tepal takes the same words. Its width over length (0.15 linear to 0.95 orbicular) is read off the chart's classes, the model's choice within them.

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.taper.note: The chart of plane shapes: ovate and lanceolate outlines are widest below the middle and narrow to the tip, obovate and spatulate ones widest above it and full to the tip, elliptic and oblong ones symmetric. Drawn as the flower card's taper powers (0.45 round to 1.3 straight to a point), the model's choice.

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.point.note: Simpson (Plant Systematics, pp. 526-527 of the PDF) classes apices of any flat part by the angle where the margins meet: acuminate under 45 degrees with hollow sides, acute 45 to 90, obtuse over 90, rounded curved. Drawn on the flower card's point, 1 to 0, the model's choice.

rules.appearance.organs.*.shape.notch.note: Kaplan's Principles of Plant Morphology describes petal tips as entire, emarginate (notched) or bilobed. How deep the card draws the notch (0.15 and 0.45 of its notch range) is the model's choice.

rules.appearance.organs.*.season.bud.note: How PlantGen draws a plant's year, a choice of the model's (development, 2026-10-14): the months a species is stated to flower in and to bear ripe fruit in (traits `flowering_months` and `fruiting_months`) set the days of each look with a season, so its flowers are open through the first and its fruit ripe through the second. Its buds show 15 days before its first flowers, about as long as the hand-set seasons this replaces gave them; a plant that flowers from January has its buds in the December before, and its year's days run on from there. A cluster's units open over its season's `opening` days, so its first goes to fruit that many days before its last; fruit ripens over its `ripening` days. A season holds one stage at a time for its first unit, so where its fruit is ripe in a month it still flowers in, the months it does both are shared out: its last flowers go to fruit in the middle of them and its fruit is drawn ripe from then, each up to a month short of the months stated.

rules.note: How PlantGen lays out an inflorescence, a choice of the model's (spec rework L1): the inflorescence characters set the cluster of any look a taxon draws as one (`"inflorescence": {}`), its kind, how many units it bears on each axis, its primary branches and how it holds itself. Sizes, stalks and spacing stay set by hand until programs size their organs from characters.

traits.bud_position.note: Barthélémy and Caraglio (2007), read in excerpts (the full text was not reachable): branches grow mostly from the upper part of their parent's annual shoot (acrotony) on each year's shoot of trees and shrubs alike, while the basitony of shrubs is the whole plant renewing from its base. Stated here, at the flowering plants, until a lineage that branches otherwise along its shoots says so.

traits.shoot_leaves.note: A typical count inferred from the few lineages counted in sources read here, until each lineage states its own. Critchfield (1971, read in full) counted 2 to 4 leaf pairs on most long shoots of striped maple and 5 to 9 on the rest, and 12 to 16 pairs on red maple's longest; aspen's first five to eight leaves are preformed in the bud and long shoots add more (from a search excerpt of an American Journal of Botany paper on aspen, not read); and the largest buds of Nothofagus pumilio hold 15 to 20 nodes (Souza and others 2000, abstract).

generator.defaults.crown_radius.why: A crown spreads about as wide, for its height, as the built-in shrubs' median, until a flora gives its width.

generator.defaults.internode.why: A larger plant grows longer shoots: an internode a tenth of the usual height grows a shrub to about that height by its last keyframe (species-spec pilot, 2026-10-14), its crown's space still topped at the greatest.

generator.defaults.path_half.why: Shoots shorten as the wood from the base lengthens, by the built-in shrubs' median share of the crown's height.

generator.defaults.leaf_size.why: A leaf card holds one leaf and its stalk: the leaf's length and about half again.

generator.defaults.spur_leaf.why: A short shoot's leaves are a little smaller than a long shoot's, by the built-in shrubs' median share (32 of them, 2026-10-16), so a species' stated leaf length sizes both.

generator.defaults.leaf_years.why: An evergreen keeps each leaf two years, the built-in evergreen broadleaves' median (2 for 8 of them, 3 for 5); a deciduous plant sheds them in its first autumn.

generator.program.note: A woody flowering plant grows by the broadleaf program; a lineage's own program, named nearer, takes its place.

generator.defaults.note: Defaults for the form where its lineage program leaves a parameter valueless: the values the lineage programs share (Oleaceae's, with extinction 0.5 and no terminal blooms), and over them the medians of the built-in species of the form (2026-10-14). They yield to a lineage program's values and to any file's.

growth.note: A shrub is grown to the age the built-in shrubs mostly are.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

appearance.note: Neutral bark and leaf greens, until a family or species states its own colours.

rules.note: Sizes a shrub takes from its own facts by the built-in shrubs' medians, and its shoots' length from its usual height so it grows to it (ten Rubiaceae of the species-spec pilot, grown at 0.89 to 1.25 times the middle of their usual heights, median 1.02), as defaults that yield to a lineage program's values and any file's.

generator.defaults.leaf_length.why: A stem's longest leaf is as long as floras measure the leaves.

generator.defaults.basal_length.why: A rosette leaf's card holds its blade and its petiole, as long as floras measure them, which for a forb with a rosette they mostly measure there.

generator.defaults.basal_leaves.why: A herb with a basal rosette has leaves at the foot of its stems, as many as the built-in rosette forbs mostly have (their median); one without, or whose taxa name no usual habit, has none.

generator.defaults.stems.why: A bulb or a corm is one shortened shoot, so it sends up one flowering stem (a bulb that has split into several is several plants); a rhizome or a cluster of tubers sends up a clump of them, as many as the herb defaults give, and so does a herb whose taxa name no usual mode of perennation.

generator.defaults.adult_age.why: An annual flowers in its first year and a biennial in its second; a perennial, or a herb whose taxa name no usual life span, from the year the lineage programs on herb mostly give.

generator.defaults.maturity.why: An annual's stems reach full size within its one season; a perennial's over the years the built-in forbs' median gives.

generator.defaults.leaf_length.why: A full-size leaf is as long on average as floras measure the leaves.

generator.defaults.stalk_height.why: A rosette's flowering stalk stands about as high as floras give the plant's usual height, which they measure in flower.

generator.defaults.trunk_radius.why: A rosette's stem is about as thick as its leaves are long allows: the built-in rosette succulents' stems are about 0.15 of their leaf length in radius.

generator.defaults.stalk_radius.why: A flowering stalk's girth goes with its height, as in the built-in rosette succulents (about 0.014 of it in radius).

generator.defaults.flower_size.why: A flower is as wide as floras measure it.

generator.defaults.internode.why: A rosette's stem gains about a six-hundredth of its leaf length with each leaf, as the built-in rosette succulents' stems do, so a small rosette stays nearly stemless.

generator.defaults.pup_distance.why: A pup roots about a leaf's length out from its parent, as the built-in rosette succulents' do (0.8 of it), so a small rosette's offsets stay close.

generator.defaults.branch_length.why: A flowering stalk's side branches go with its height, as in the built-in rosette succulents (about 0.18 of it).
